newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Earthquake rocks eastern Taiwan, no damage reported.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake rocks eastern Taiwan, no damage reported.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.7 on the Richter scale rattled eastern Taiwan on Tuesday, but there were no immediate reports of injuries or damage, officials said.
The quake's epicentre was 21.7 km (13.5 miles) due north of eastern coastal town of Hualien and 21.3 km (13.2 miles) beneath the earth's surface.
There were no immediate reports of damage or casualties from the tremor, the interior ministry said.
The quake shook buildings in the capital Taipei and was felt in most parts of the island.
Its highest magnitude on land was four on the Richter scale recorded in Hualien.
Earthquakes are relatively common on the island but rarely cause major damage.
